summary: Leros Airport (IATA: LRS, ICAO: LGLE) is a small domestic airport located on the eastern side of Leros Island in Greece's Dodecanese archipelago. The airport primarily serves short-haul Olympic Air and Sky Express flights connecting Leros with Athens and other nearby islands. Its modest size and scenic setting make it a charming gateway to one of the most unspoiled islands in the Aegean.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Leros Airport to the main towns on the island?
A: Taxis are typically available outside the terminal to take you to Lakki, Agia Marina, or Platanos within 10-15 minutes.

Q: Are there direct flights to Leros from Athens?
A: Yes, Olympic Air and Sky Express operate regular scheduled flights between Athens Eleftherios Venizelos Airport and Leros.

Q: Does Leros Airport operate international flights?
A: No, the airport handles only domestic flights, primarily from Athens and occasionally from neighboring Dodecanese islands like Kos and Rhodes.

Q: Is there car rental available at the airport?
A: Car and scooter rental services are available on Leros, though booking in advance is recommended as on-site options may be limited.
transport_tips: Taxis wait outside the small terminal and are the most reliable way to reach Lakki, Agia Marina, or Platanos, all within a short drive. There is no public bus service directly serving the airport, so arranging private transfer or rental in advance is wise. If arriving on a late flight, consider pre-booking accommodation transfer as taxi availability can be limited after evening arrivals.
local_tip: The airport sits on a plateau with panoramic views over the Aegean — take a window seat on departure or arrival to spot the historic windmills of Lakki and the Turkish coast in the distance.
